title: Reverse the Text Inside Parentheses

concept.title: Each open bracket starts a new piece of text
body: The text has nested parentheses. The text inside every pair must be **reversed**, working from the **innermost** pair outwards, and the parentheses are removed. In `(ed(et)oc)el`: reverse `et` to `te`, giving `(edteoc)el`, then reverse `edteoc` to `coetde`, and so on.

A stack of strings does it in one pass. Keep the current text `cur`. On `(`: **push** `cur` on the stack and start a new empty `cur` (the text inside). On `)`: the inside is complete, **reverse** it, pop the saved text and put the reversed inside after it: `cur = saved + reversed(cur)`. Letters are appended to `cur`.

body.code:
stack = []; cur = ""
for ch in s:
    if ch == "(":   stack.append(cur); cur = ""
    elif ch == ")": cur = stack.pop() + cur[::-1]
    else:           cur += ch

body: Each level is reversed exactly once for each pair that contains it, which is correct: a letter inside two pairs is reversed twice.

statement: A word contains lowercase letters and balanced parentheses. Reverse the text inside every pair of matching parentheses, starting with the innermost pairs, and remove all the parentheses. Print the result, or `empty` if nothing remains.

examples.note: The inner et becomes te, then edteoc becomes coetde: coetdeel.

hints: Use a stack of strings: one saved text for every open bracket.
On `(` push the current text and start a new one.
On `)` reverse the current text and attach it to the text taken from the stack.

explanation: The stack keeps the text of the outer levels. A closing bracket reverses the finished inner text and glues it behind the saved outer text.
solution.complexity: Time O(n^2) in the worst case (deep nesting), space O(n).
